product.title: Venture Capital Tycoon
product.summary: Run a fifty-million-dollar venture fund across five years.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students review deal flow each year and choose to invest or pass, then in portfolio review add follow-on capital or cut losers, then decide whether to sell now or hold for a riskier payout, while market news shifts sector valuations. The final score blends fund return with a scorecard of the economic reasoning used.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Complete and publicly reachable. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. Five years of portfolio construction with real market events and a concept scorecard. Passing on everything is correctly punished — 1.00x and a D against 6.82x and a B for an active strategy — but two defects undercut the model's credibility.
knownBlockers: A visible arithmetic error in an economics product: a startup valued at $3.0M asking $6.2M reported "Invested $6.2M for 207% equity". Equity is never clamped, and a second fresh run reproduced the asking-above-valuation pattern on a different deal.

The Key Takeaways text is templated rather than derived from play. A run that made zero investments in five years was still praised for "Exit Timing" and for acting "decisively on opportunities", and was told "Good job cutting losers!" directly beneath a D grade for Sunk Cost Awareness.
